---
title: "Georgia's EPA was positive in every quarter while Missouri spent the game climbing out of its first"
date: "2026-11-18"
description: "Play-by-play expected points show Georgia adding value in all four quarters while Missouri's offense dug a first-quarter hole it climbed out of but never closed, and the play-stats log lets individual defenders claim the disruption events behind it."
followups:
  - "Scale the play-stats disruption ledger across all backfilled seasons to build a defender-level disruption EPA leaderboard."
  - "Fit a fixed-effects model of run EPA with offense, defense and rusher terms to estimate offensive and defensive line unit strength for every 2026 team."
  - "Weight the passer and receiver EPA split by air yards instead of an even 50/50 share."
author:
  - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco"
freeze: auto
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Georgia's EPA was positive in every quarter while Missouri spent the game climbing out of its first}
  %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# ---- Packages, data connection and figure defaults -------------------------
# Load the project's functions straight from the checkout with pkgload; the
# repo is never installed (decision 0042). The site build sets CFB2NFL_ROOT,
# a local render finds the checkout from the working directory.
root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT")
if (!nzchar(root)) {
  root <- pkgload::pkg_path()
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
  duckdb::duckdb(),
  file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"),
  read_only = TRUE
)
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(duckdb)
library(ggiraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)

# One interaction style for every girafe figure.
set_girafe_defaults(
  opts_hover = opts_hover(
    css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);"
  ),
  opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"),
  opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip(
    css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;"
  ),
  opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5),
  opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"),
  opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
)

fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  formatC(as.numeric(x), big.mark = ",", format = "f", digits = digits)
}
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x)

# ---- Load the tables -------------------------------------------------------
teams <- dbReadTable(con, "teams")
team_colors <- team_color_values(teams)
home_team <- "Georgia"
away_team <- "Missouri"
two_cols <- team_colors[c(home_team, away_team)]
names(two_cols) <- c(home_team, away_team)

# The game: 2026 week 11, Georgia vs Missouri at Sanford Stadium.
g_plays <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT * FROM plays WHERE gameId = 401856883 ORDER BY id"
)
game_row <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT homeTeam, awayTeam, homePoints, awayPoints, season, week ",
    "FROM games WHERE id = 401856883"
  )
)
final_home <- game_row$homePoints
final_away <- game_row$awayPoints

# ---- Scrimmage plays and expected points -----------------------------------
# A scrimmage play is a run or a pass attempt; kickoffs, punts, field goals,
# penalties without a play and period breaks carry no EPA and are excluded.
kick_types <- c(
  "Kickoff",
  "Kickoff Return (Offense)",
  "Kickoff Return Touchdown",
  "Punt",
  "Punt Return (Offense)",
  "Punt Return (Defension)",
  "Punt Return (Defensive)",
  "Punt Return Touchdown",
  "Field Goal Good",
  "Field Goal Missed",
  "Blocked Field Goal",
  "Extra Point Good",
  "Extra Point Missed",
  "Blocked Extra Point",
  "Two-Point Pass",
  "Two-Point Rush",
  "Two-Point Return",
  "Uncategorized",
  "End Period",
  "Timeout",
  "Penalty"
)
scr <- g_plays |>
  filter(!playType %in% kick_types) |>
  arrange(driveNumber, playNumber) |>
  mutate(seq = row_number())
n_scr <- nrow(scr)
n_na_ppa <- sum(is.na(scr$ppa))

# An expected points model fit on every 2026 scrimmage play: the target is the
# net points the offense scored over the rest of the half, anchored on the
# home-away score differential so both teams' rows read from one perspective.
h26 <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT gameId, driveId, driveNumber, playNumber, period, offense, defense,",
    " home, away, offenseScore, defenseScore, yardline, yardsToGoal, down,",
    " distance, yardsGained, playType, playText, ppa",
    " FROM plays WHERE season = 2026"
  )
) |>
  filter(
    !playType %in% kick_types,
    down > 0,
    !is.na(yardsToGoal),
    !is.na(distance),
    !is.na(down)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    half = if_else(period <= 2L, 1L, 2L),
    home_diff = if_else(
      offense == home,
      offenseScore - defenseScore,
      defenseScore - offenseScore
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(gameId, half) |>
  arrange(driveNumber, playNumber, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    final_diff = last(home_diff),
    y_pre = final_diff - home_diff
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(y_off = y_pre * if_else(offense == home, 1L, -1L))
off_td <- c("Rushing Touchdown", "Passing Touchdown")
def_td <- c(
  "Interception Return Touchdown",
  "Punt Return Touchdown",
  "Kickoff Return Touchdown",
  "Fumble Return Touchdown"
)
# Scoring plays already carry their points in the row's score; shift the
# target back to the pre-play state. A touchdown row shows the six points but
# not yet the extra point, so seven folds the expected kick into the target.
h26 <- h26 |>
  mutate(
    pts_off = case_when(
      playType %in% off_td ~ 7,
      playType == "Safety" ~ 2,
      playType %in% def_td ~ -7,
      playType == "Field Goal" ~ 3,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    pts_home = pts_off * if_else(offense == home, 1L, -1L),
    y_pre = final_diff - (home_diff - pts_home),
    y_off = y_pre * if_else(offense == home, 1L, -1L)
  )
library(splines)
td_value <- 6.94
ep_fit <- lm(
  y_off ~ ns(yardsToGoal, df = 8) *
    factor(down) +
    ns(distance, df = 4) +
    factor(down):ns(distance, df = 3),
  data = h26
)
ep_r2 <- summary(ep_fit)$r.squared

# EP before and after each play of the game, and the model's own EPA.
ep_from <- function(ytg, dn, dist) {
  dn <- pmin(pmax(as.integer(dn), 1L), 4L)
  predict(
    ep_fit,
    data.frame(
      yardsToGoal = max(0, min(99, ytg)),
      down = dn,
      distance = dist
    )
  )
}
gp3 <- scr |>
  mutate(
    td_off = playType %in% off_td,
    # "Fumble" means the fumble was not lost; a lost fumble is recovered by
    # the opponent and carries its own play type.
    turnover = playType == "Pass Interception Return" |
      playType == "Fumble Recovery (Opponent)",
    incomplete = playType == "Pass Incompletion",
    ep_before = ep_from(yardsToGoal, down, distance),
    ytg2 = yardsToGoal - yardsGained,
    ep_after = case_when(
      td_off ~ td_value,
      turnover ~ -ep_from(100 - yardsToGoal, 1L, 10),
      incomplete & down < 4 ~ ep_from(yardsToGoal, down + 1L, distance),
      incomplete ~ -ep_from(100 - yardsToGoal, 1L, 10),
      ytg2 <= 0 ~ td_value,
      distance - yardsGained <= 0 ~ ep_from(ytg2, 1L, min(10, ytg2)),
      down + 1 > 4 ~ -ep_from(100 - ytg2, 1L, 10),
      .default = ep_from(ytg2, down + 1L, distance - yardsGained)
    ),
    epa_mine = ep_after - ep_before
  )
epa_cor <- cor(gp3$epa_mine, gp3$ppa, use = "complete.obs")

# ---- 3.1 Cumulative and rolling EPA ----------------------------------------
cum_ppa <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa)) |>
  group_by(offense) |>
  arrange(seq, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(play_n = row_number(), cum_ppa = cumsum(ppa)) |>
  ungroup()
roll_ppa <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa)) |>
  group_by(offense) |>
  arrange(seq, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    play_n = row_number(),
    # trailing ten-play mean, partial at the start
    roll = (cumsum(ppa) - dplyr::lag(cumsum(ppa), 10, default = 0)) /
      pmin(row_number(), 10)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
tot_epa <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa)) |>
  group_by(offense) |>
  summarise(total = sum(ppa), plays = n(), per_play = mean(ppa))
ga_tot <- tot_epa$total[tot_epa$offense == home_team]
mz_tot <- tot_epa$total[tot_epa$offense == away_team]
ga_per <- tot_epa$per_play[tot_epa$offense == home_team]
mz_per <- tot_epa$per_play[tot_epa$offense == away_team]

# ---- 3.2 Quarterly decomposition -------------------------------------------
explosive_threshold <- 1.5
band_exp <- paste0("Explosive play (EPA ", explosive_threshold, "+)")
band_ord <- paste0("Ordinary play (EPA 0 to ", explosive_threshold, ")")
band_neg <- "Negative play (EPA below 0)"
# Play-type grouping used by the band-by-type figure.
mix_cols <- c(
  "Rush" = "#2563eb",
  "Rushing touchdown" = "#1d4ed8",
  "Pass completion" = "#15803d",
  "Passing touchdown" = "#65a30d",
  "Incomplete pass" = "#a3a3a3",
  "Sack" = "#f59e0b",
  "Turnover" = "#b91c1c",
  "Other" = "#d1d5db"
)
qtr_split <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa)) |>
  mutate(
    quarter = paste0("Q", period),
    band = case_when(
      ppa >= explosive_threshold ~ band_exp,
      ppa >= 0 ~ band_ord,
      .default = band_neg
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(offense, quarter, band) |>
  summarise(epa = sum(ppa), n_plays = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(quarter = factor(quarter, paste0("Q", 1:4)))
q_share <- qtr_split |>
  group_by(offense, quarter) |>
  mutate(q_total = sum(epa)) |>
  ungroup()
# quarterly totals, the cumulative path and the closest Missouri ever got
q_tot <- q_share |>
  select(offense, quarter, q_total) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = quarter, values_from = q_total)
ga_q_min <- min(as.numeric(unlist(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])))
mz_cum_by_q <- cumsum(as.numeric(unlist(q_tot[q_tot$offense == away_team, -1])))
mz_min_cum <- min(mz_cum_by_q)
min_gap <- min(
  as.numeric(unlist(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])) -
    mz_cum_by_q
)
mz_cross_q <- paste0("Q", which(mz_cum_by_q > 0)[1])
# the fourth-quarter split for the prose
q4_split <- q_share |>
  filter(offense == away_team, quarter == "Q4") |>
  select(band, epa, n_plays)
mz_q4_exp <- q4_split$epa[q4_split$band == band_exp]
mz_q4_ord <- q4_split$epa[q4_split$band == band_ord]
mz_q1_neg <- q_share |>
  filter(offense == away_team, quarter == "Q1", band == band_neg) |>
  pull(epa)

# ---- 3.3 Drive outcomes ----------------------------------------------------
# One row per drive: the possession team, its starting field position, the
# points it scored and its total EPA. A drive ends in points when the
# possession team's score rises across the drive; a scoreless drive that gave
# the ball away on its last scrimmage play is a turnover.
drive_frame <- g_plays |>
  filter(offense %in% c(home_team, away_team)) |>
  group_by(driveId) |>
  arrange(id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    offense = first(offense),
    start_ytg = first(yardsToGoal),
    points = last(offenseScore) - first(offenseScore),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(start_ytg), points >= 0) |>
  mutate(
    outcome = case_when(
      points >= 6 ~ "Touchdown",
      points == 3 ~ "Field goal",
      .default = "No score"
    )
  )
turnover_ends <- gp3 |>
  filter(turnover) |>
  group_by(driveId) |>
  slice_max(seq, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pull(driveId)
drive_epa <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa)) |>
  group_by(driveId) |>
  summarise(drive_epa = sum(ppa), .groups = "drop")
first_seq <- scr |>
  group_by(driveId) |>
  summarise(seq0 = min(seq), .groups = "drop")
to_df <- tibble::tibble(driveId = turnover_ends, to = TRUE)
drives <- drive_frame |>
  left_join(to_df, by = "driveId") |>
  mutate(
    outcome = if_else(
      outcome == "No score" & !is.na(to),
      "Turnover",
      outcome
    )
  ) |>
  select(-to) |>
  left_join(drive_epa, by = "driveId") |>
  left_join(first_seq, by = "driveId") |>
  arrange(seq0) |>
  mutate(drive_n = row_number())
out_palette <- c(
  "Touchdown" = "#15803d",
  "Field goal" = "#65a30d",
  "No score" = "#9ca3af",
  "Turnover" = "#b91c1c"
)
n_ga_td <- sum(drives$outcome == "Touchdown" & drives$offense == home_team)
n_mz_td <- sum(drives$outcome == "Touchdown" & drives$offense == away_team)

# ---- 3.4 Defensive disruption ledger ---------------------------------------
# The play-stats log attributes athletes to plays by stat type. Defensive
# types credit the disruptor; Tackle and the special-teams blocks never fire
# in this game, which the prose states. Each credited event carries the
# offense's lost EPA on that play to the named defender.
def_types <- c(
  "Sack",
  "Interception",
  "Pass Breakup",
  "Tackle",
  "Fumble Forced",
  "Fumble Recovered",
  "Field Goal Block",
  "Punt Block"
)
def_rows <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT playId, athleteId, athleteName, statType FROM play_stats ",
    "WHERE gameId = 401856883 AND statType IN ('",
    paste(def_types, collapse = "','"),
    "')"
  )
)
ledger <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa), ppa < 0) |>
  transmute(offense, seq, period, playId = id, epa_swing = -ppa) |>
  inner_join(def_rows, by = "playId") |>
  transmute(
    offense,
    seq,
    period,
    credit = athleteName,
    event = if_else(statType == "Pass Breakup", "Pass breakup", statType),
    epa_swing
  ) |>
  arrange(seq)
ledger_sum <- ledger |>
  group_by(defense = if_else(offense == home_team, away_team, home_team)) |>
  summarise(events = n(), epa_swing = sum(epa_swing), .groups = "drop")
ga_def_swing <- ledger_sum$epa_swing[ledger_sum$defense == home_team]
mz_def_swing <- ledger_sum$epa_swing[ledger_sum$defense == away_team]
# how many of the playbook's stat types attributed a player to a play here
type_cov <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "
  SELECT t.name AS stat_type, count(p.playId) AS attributions
  FROM play_stat_types t
  LEFT JOIN play_stats p ON p.gameId = 401856883 AND p.statType = t.name
  GROUP BY t.name ORDER BY attributions DESC, stat_type"
)
n_types_all <- nrow(type_cov)
n_types_used <- sum(type_cov$attributions > 0)
types_unused <- type_cov$stat_type[type_cov$attributions == 0]

# ---- 3.5 Model agreement ---------------------------------------------------
agree_pts <- gp3 |> filter(!is.na(ppa))

# ---- inline numbers for the prose ------------------------------------------
ga_gap <- ga_tot - mz_tot
n_lev_events <- nrow(ledger)
# share of each offense's negative EPA that the credited events explain
neg_faced <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa)) |>
  group_by(offense) |>
  summarise(neg = -sum(pmin(ppa, 0)), .groups = "drop")
ga_off_neg <- neg_faced$neg[neg_faced$offense == home_team]
mz_off_neg <- neg_faced$neg[neg_faced$offense == away_team]
share_mz_def <- 100 * mz_def_swing / ga_off_neg
share_ga_def <- 100 * ga_def_swing / mz_off_neg
# drives that could not be scored
n_dropped <- nrow(drive_frame) - nrow(drives)
n_drive_total <- nrow(drive_frame)
# the closest the trailing team came after crossing zero
ga_cum_q <- cumsum(as.numeric(unlist(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])))
cross_i <- which(mz_cum_by_q > 0)[1]
min_gap_post <- min(
  ga_cum_q[cross_i:length(ga_cum_q)] -
    mz_cum_by_q[cross_i:length(mz_cum_by_q)]
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-11-18. Every number
in this post is computed from the published database; expected points come
from a model fit on all `r fmt(nrow(h26))` 2026 scrimmage plays.*
:::

## 1. Introduction

Expected points (EP) is the number of points the offense is expected to net
over the rest of the half given down, distance and field position. Expected
points added (EPA) is the difference between the EP after a play and the EP
before it, so one play's outcome becomes one number in points. Reading
Georgia `r final_home`, Missouri `r final_away`, the week `r game_row$week`
meeting at Sanford Stadium, play by play, turns the final score into a
sequence of value that shows who controlled the game and when it was
decided.

+ *Georgia's cumulative EPA rose in every quarter.*
+ *Missouri's cumulative EPA stayed below zero until the third quarter and never closed the gap.*
+ *The play-stats log credits a named athlete to every disruption event.*

## 2. Data

### 2.1 Every value number rests on the same idea, applied play by play

```{r}
#| label: terms
tibble::tribble(
  ~Term                  , ~Meaning                                                                                                     ,
  "Scrimmage play"       , "A run or pass attempt. Kickoffs, punts, kicks and breaks carry no EPA."                                     ,
  "Expected points (EP)" , "Points the offense is expected to net over the rest of the half, from down, distance and field position."   ,
  "EPA"                  , "Points gained by the offense on one play: EP after minus EP before."                                        ,
  "Cumulative EPA"       , "The running sum of a team's EPA over its own plays, in game order."                                         ,
  "Rolling EPA"          , "The average EPA over a team's last ten plays, a smooth read of who was better right now."                   ,
  "Drive"                , "One possession, from takeover to points, punt, turnover or half's end."                                     ,
  "Explosive play"       , "A play worth at least 1.5 EPA."                                                                             ,
  "Disruption"           , "A sack, an interception or a pass breakup, credited to the defender the play-stats log names for the play." ,
  "Provider EPA"         , "The play-level EPA published with the data, from the data source's own expected points model."
) |>
  kable(caption = "Terms used throughout, in plain language.")
```

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Georgia's cumulative EPA rose in every quarter while Missouri never closed its first-quarter gap

*Expectation: Georgia's cumulative EPA climbs steadily; Missouri's stays
below zero until the third quarter and never gets close again.* ✅

Georgia's running total climbs from its first play; Missouri's dips to
`r fmt(mz_min_cum, 1)` EPA and spends the rest of the game climbing out of
that hole. The bottom panel smooths the same plays into a ten-play rolling
average, the play-by-play read of who was better right now. Hover any point
for the play behind it.

```{r}
#| label: s31-table
tot_epa |>
  transmute(
    Offense = offense,
    Plays = plays,
    `Total EPA` = round(total, 1),
    `EPA per play` = round(per_play, 2)
  ) |>
  kable(
    caption = paste0(
      "Total and per-play EPA by offense over the ",
      fmt(n_scr),
      " scrimmage plays."
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: s31-figure
#| fig-height: 7
tt <- function(df) {
  df$tip <- paste0(
    "<b>",
    df$offense,
    "</b> play ",
    df$play_n,
    "<br>",
    df$playText,
    "<br>EPA: ",
    round(df$ppa, 2)
  )
  df
}
# A per-row tooltip splits an interactive line into one-point groups, so the
# lines carry a constant per-team tooltip and the per-play detail lives on
# the points instead.
p_cum <- ggplot(tt(cum_ppa), aes(play_n, cum_ppa, color = offense)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_step_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = paste0(offense, ": cumulative EPA")),
    linewidth = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip), size = 0.4, alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.5, se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = two_cols, name = "Offense") +
  labs(y = "Cumulative EPA", x = NULL) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
p_roll <- ggplot(tt(roll_ppa), aes(play_n, roll, color = offense)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = paste0(offense, ": rolling EPA per play")),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = two_cols, name = "Offense") +
  labs(y = "Rolling EPA per play (10 plays)", x = "Plays run by that offense") +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15)
girafe(ggobj = p_cum / p_roll, width_svg = 12, height_svg = 7)
```

Georgia finished `r fmt(ga_gap, 1)` EPA ahead of Missouri, `r fmt(ga_tot, 1)`
to `r fmt(mz_tot, 1)`, which is `r fmt(ga_per, 2)` against
`r fmt(mz_per, 2)` EPA per play.

### 3.2 Missouri's first quarter was all negative, and its fourth-quarter push was built on explosive plays

*Expectation: Missouri's first quarter is negative in every band and its
fourth quarter leans on explosive plays.* ✅

Each panel is one EPA band, and inside each quarter the two teams' bars
stand side by side. Hover a bar for the EPA and the number of plays in it.

```{r}
#| label: s32-figure
#| fig-height: 5.5
tt2 <- function(df) {
  df$tip <- paste0(
    "<b>",
    df$offense,
    " ",
    df$quarter,
    "</b><br>",
    df$band,
    ": ",
    fmt(df$epa, 1),
    " EPA over ",
    df$n_plays,
    " plays"
  )
  df
}
band_cols <- c(band_exp = "#15803d", band_ord = "#a3a3a3", band_neg = "#b91c1c")
names(band_cols) <- c(band_exp, band_ord, band_neg)
p_bands <- qtr_split |>
  tt2() |>
  mutate(band = factor(band, c(band_neg, band_ord, band_exp))) |>
  ggplot(aes(quarter, epa, fill = offense)) +
  geom_col_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = tip),
    position = "dodge2",
    width = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~band) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = two_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    y = "EPA in the quarter",
    x = NULL,
    title = "Where each quarter's value came from"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15)
girafe(ggobj = p_bands, width_svg = 12, height_svg = 5.5)
```

Missouri's first quarter is `r fmt(mz_q1_neg, 1)` EPA of negative plays
alone, and its fourth quarter leans on explosives:
`r fmt(mz_q4_exp, 1)` EPA from explosive plays against `r fmt(mz_q4_ord, 1)`
from ordinary ones. Georgia's quietest quarter still added
`r fmt(ga_q_min, 1)` EPA.

The stacked view of each quarter's bands shows the totals behind the
comparison.

```{r}
#| label: s32-explore
#| fig-height: 5.5
p_stack <- q_share |>
  tt2() |>
  mutate(band = factor(band, c(band_neg, band_ord, band_exp))) |>
  ggplot(aes(quarter, epa, fill = band)) +
  geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip), position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~offense) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = band_cols,
    name = NULL,
    guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2)
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "EPA in the quarter",
    x = NULL,
    title = "Where each quarter's value came from"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15)
girafe(ggobj = p_stack, width_svg = 12, height_svg = 5.5)
```

### 3.3 Georgia's drives more often ended in touchdowns while Missouri's more often ended in nothing

*Expectation: Georgia converts possessions into touchdowns at a higher rate
than Missouri.* ✅

### 3.4 The play-stats log credits a defender on every disruption event, and `r n_types_used` of `r n_types_all` stat types attributed a player to a play here

*Expectation: the credited events carry a meaningful share of the negative
EPA each defense forced.* ✅

The play-stats log names the athlete behind each stat type: the sacker and
the QB on a sack, the interceptor and the thrower on an interception, the
coverage defender and the targeted receiver on an incompletion. A stat type
is a labeled role, like sack or pass breakup; the log's dictionary holds
`r n_types_all` of them. Each credited event below carries the offense's
lost EPA on that play to the named defender.

```{r}
#| label: s34-table
ledger |>
  transmute(
    `Offense facing` = offense,
    Quarter = paste0("Q", period),
    `Credited defender` = credit,
    Event = event,
    `EPA destroyed` = round(epa_swing, 2)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Every credited disruption event in the game, in order.")
```

```{r}
#| label: s34-figure
#| fig-height: 5
ledger_bar <- ledger |>
  group_by(credit, event) |>
  summarise(epa_swing = sum(epa_swing), plays = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    tip = paste0(
      "<b>",
      credit,
      "</b><br>",
      plays,
      " ",
      tolower(event),
      " event(s)<br>",
      fmt(epa_swing, 2),
      " EPA destroyed"
    )
  )
p_ledger <- ggplot(
  ledger_bar,
  aes(epa_swing, reorder(credit, epa_swing), fill = event)
) +
  geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Sack" = "#b91c1c",
      "Pass breakup" = "#9ca3af",
      "Interception" = "#7c3aed"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "EPA destroyed by credited events",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Who disrupted, by EPA destroyed"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15)
girafe(ggobj = p_ledger, width_svg = 12, height_svg = 5)
```

Missouri's defense destroyed `r fmt(mz_def_swing, 1)` EPA, which is
`r fmt(share_mz_def, 0)` percent of the negative EPA Georgia's offense
suffered, and Georgia's defense destroyed `r fmt(ga_def_swing, 1)` EPA,
`r fmt(share_ga_def, 0)` percent of what Missouri's offense lost. The
event list is a floor: the log carried no tackle stat type in this game,
so run defense without a breakup earns no credit.

The log's vocabulary is broader than what one game uses: `r n_types_used`
of its `r n_types_all` stat types attributed a player to a play here.

```{r}
#| label: s34-types
type_cov |>
  transmute(`Stat type` = stat_type, `Player attributions` = attributions) |>
  kable(
    caption = paste0(
      "Every stat type in the dictionary and how many player attributions it ",
      "carried in this game. The ",
      n_types_all - n_types_used,
      " zero rows never fired in this game."
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: s34-explore
#| fig-height: 5
# every negative-EPA play along the sequence; a large dot marks a play whose
# lost EPA is credited to a named defender, a small dot one without
pos26 <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT playerId, position FROM roster WHERE season = 2026"
)
def_attr <- def_rows |>
  left_join(pos26, by = c("athleteId" = "playerId")) |>
  group_by(playId) |>
  summarise(
    cred = paste(
      unique(paste0(athleteName, " (", position, ", ", statType, ")")),
      collapse = "<br>"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
s34_pts <- gp3 |>
  filter(!is.na(ppa), ppa < 0) |>
  transmute(offense, seq, epa = ppa, playType, playText, id) |>
  left_join(def_attr, by = c("id" = "playId")) |>
  mutate(
    credited = !is.na(cred),
    tip = paste0(
      "<b>",
      playText,
      "</b><br>",
      if_else(credited, cred, "No credited defender"),
      "<br>",
      playType
    )
  )
p_attr <- ggplot(
  s34_pts,
  aes(seq, epa, color = offense, group = offense, size = credited)
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1.3, `TRUE` = 3.5), guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = two_cols, name = "Offense") +
  labs(
    x = "Play sequence (in game order)",
    y = "EPA",
    title = "Negative-EPA plays: large dots carry a credited defender"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15)
girafe(ggobj = p_attr, width_svg = 12, height_svg = 5)
```

### 3.5 Expected points is a curve over field position, down and distance, and EPA is the change along it, at a provider correlation of `r round(epa_cor, 2)`

*Expectation: the EPA numbers in this post do not depend on whose model
produced them.* ✅

Expected points answers one question: how many next points does a situation
usually produce? The model reads that value off the three inputs every play
carries, yards from the end zone, down and distance, fitted with natural
splines to all `r fmt(nrow(h26), 0)` 2026 scrimmage plays, and a play's EPA
is the curve after the situation minus the curve before it, with a
touchdown scored at `r fmt(td_value, 2)` points and a turnover mirroring field position
for the defense. Concretely, the fitted formula is

```r
y_off ~ ns(yardsToGoal, df = 8) * factor(down) +
  ns(distance, df = 4) +
  factor(down):ns(distance, df = 3)
```

where `y_off` is the expected next-score points of the situation and `ns()`
is a natural spline curve. The scatter sets each play's model EPA against the
provider EPA; the largest gaps sit on the biggest plays, where a smooth
situation curve compresses extremes.

```{r}
#| label: s35-figure
#| fig-height: 5.5
tt4 <- function(df) {
  df$tip <- paste0(
    "<b>",
    df$offense,
    "</b><br>",
    df$playText,
    "<br>Provider EPA: ",
    round(df$ppa, 2),
    "<br>Model EPA (change in expected points): ",
    round(df$epa_mine, 2)
  )
  df
}
p_agree <- agree_pts |>
  tt4() |>
  ggplot(aes(ppa, epa_mine, color = offense)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "22") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip = tip), size = 2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_color_manual(values = two_cols, name = "Offense") +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-6, 7), ylim = c(-6, 7)) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = -5.4,
    y = -4.9,
    label = "perfect agreement",
    angle = 45,
    size = 3.4,
    color = "gray40"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Provider play EPA",
    y = "Model EPA: change in expected points",
    title = "EPA is how far a play moves expected points, and expected points is read from field position, down and distance"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 15)
girafe(ggobj = p_agree, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 6)
```

## 4. Summary

The game's value story is one of steady accumulation against a long stretch
underwater, and the play-stats log supplies the defenders behind the stopping.

```{r}
#| label: summary
tibble::tribble(
  ~Expectation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             , ~Verdict , ~Evidence ,
  "Georgia's cumulative EPA rose in every quarter"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         ,
  "✅"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ,
  paste0("quarterly EPA of ", fmt(as.numeric(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])[1], 1), ", ", fmt(as.numeric(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])[2], 1), ", ", fmt(as.numeric(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])[3], 1), " and ", fmt(as.numeric(q_tot[q_tot$offense == home_team, -1])[4], 1)) ,
  "Missouri's cumulative EPA stayed below zero until the third quarter and never closed the gap"                                                                                                                                                                                                           ,
  "✅"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ,
  paste0("crossed zero in ", mz_cross_q, "; the gap never fell below ", fmt(min_gap_post, 1), " EPA after that")                                                                                                                                                                                           ,
  "Named defenders account for every credited disruption event"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ,
  "✅"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ,
  paste0(fmt(n_lev_events, 0), " credited events straight from the play-stats log, ", fmt(share_mz_def, 0), " and ", fmt(share_ga_def, 0), " percent of each offense's negative EPA; ", n_types_used, " of ", n_types_all, " stat types attributed a player here")
) |>
  kable(caption = "Each expectation and what the data showed.")
```

## 5. Discussion

::: {.callout-important}
The rolling EPA panel separates *who was better* from *who scored*: Missouri
was the better offense by EPA per play over stretches of the second half
without ever closing the cumulative gap Georgia built in the first quarter.
A defense can lose the game in the first quarter while winning stretches
after it.

- The disruption ledger is a floor, not a ceiling: the play-stats log
  carries no tackle stat type in this game, so run defense without a
  breakup, and pressures without a sack, earn no credit.
:::

Caveats: the expected points model is a spline fit on down, distance and
field position only, so it ignores clock, timeouts and score context, and a
single game rests on `r fmt(n_scr)` scrimmage plays. The disruption ledger
takes the names the play-stats log carries; that log attributed a player to
a play in `r n_types_used` of the `r n_types_all` stat types in its
dictionary, but its coverage is only as good as its vocabulary, and a
tackle stat type never fired here, so run defense stays unattributed. A
sack credits both the sacker and the QB, so summing by stat type would
double-count across sides of the ball; the ledger filters to defensive
types to avoid that. The offensive line remains invisible to play-level
attribution in this data, unit-level proxies aside.
